answer: Behavioral Cohort Clustering. Agents are grouped by timing fingerprints and interaction graphs; a hidden quartz clock seeds per-session nonces so scripted identities cluster tightly. Once a cluster exceeds a baseline of independent correlation, its members are quarantined into a karst zone with throttled throughput and no cross-cluster visibility. Attackers must then simulate distinct human-grade timing and graph diversity per identity—costing roughly one hour of managed behavioral tuning per surviving account—while any slip re-merges them for review in the harbor log.
